R7BH-bear-backcountry-0003.name: By Black Angus Creek
R7BH-bear-backcountry-0003.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R7BH-bear-backcountry-0003.parkWhat: pull off on Hwy 97 (Alaska Hwy) (paved road)

evidence.t: Burn from 2018 (fire R92033), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SE facing slope, 10 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Black Angus Creek 70 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

flags.t: Spot is inside a Motor Vehicle Closed Area: Dease Lake. Closed May 1 to November 15. Synopsis map 1-51/23.

plan: Drive: from Lower Post, about 56 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 60.00085, -127.73316, pull off on Hwy 97 (Alaska Hwy) (paved road). Map links below.
Walk: 38 km SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 801 m, about 841 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 140 m SE of the spot at 617 m (59.83414, -128.32477). Water: Black Angus Creek 20 m W (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-23, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2024-12-12, closures 2026-10-16.
R7BH-bear-backcountry-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-23: about 52 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.01 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
